data.name: Pinball HD Collection
data.detailed_description:
Pinball HD Collection - This game will change your idea of Pinball. Each table - Wild West, The Deep, Jungle Style, Pirates, Red Planet, Snow, Da Vinci, Arcade, Tanks, Halloween and others - are masterpieces. You'll be stunned with the level of realism. This is a REAL Pinball simulator with stunning 3D graphics both with or without 3D glasses.

FEATURES

• Many pinball tables with unique graphics, instructions, missions system, locations and characters
• Unique soundtracks with atmospheric music, sound effects and voices.
• Realistic physics.
• Built in help with detailing instructions and descriptions of the features of each table.
• Local and global (Steam Leaderboards) high scores.
• Stereoscopic imaging option (requires anaglyph eyeglasses). You can choose between red-cyan, green-magenta or yellow-blue lenses.

reviews.review:
Basically, if you're a digital pinball collector and/or looking for some variety, you might want to get this. I'm actually finding it fairly enjoyable.

There are 15 tables with a variety of themes for $20. That's a reasonable price per table. Yes, this is a mobile port, and it shows.

The physics are very basic (think Space Cadet, but a bit better), and the designs vary in complexity from very simple to moderately complex.

You'll absolutely need to apply anti-lag tweaks, and you'll probably also want to force AA/AF externally.

The 3D graphics are reasonable, but mostly nothing special. The art is quite good, including some decent animations in places. Textures are somewhat low low res and models are low poly, though. No fancy lighting here, but there are some reflections. The graphics/art of the game look much better when you're using the dynamic camera.

There is no controller support or key rebinding. The game doesn't even tell you what the controls are! But I just use JoyToKey, that's not a deal breaker in this case. Controls are left/right arrow for flippers, down arrow for launcher, space for nudge (just upward), C for camera change. R switches to portrait orientation.

There are 3 camera views - top down, angled, and dynamic.

Nudging, as mentioned, exists, but you can only nudge upward. This is basically enough for a nudge pass. There's a tilt system with warnings on a timer (I think), but it takes more than one nudge to trigger a warning.

Dead bounces somewhat work, but are not terribly reliable. Hold passes work on some tables.

Bang backs also work quite reliably on most tables.

The flipper gap is quite small, making slap saves rather effective.

There is multiball (possibly on all tables). I've seen up to 5 balls.

There are kickbacks that are on by default, can be depleted and re-raised, at least on the tables I've played.

Tables typically will have a mix of passive progressive elements and (simple) goal oriented modes. There are some video modes too. There's a decent variety of playfield elements, including extra flippers and playfields. Extra balls are awarded at certain score thresholds. Some tables have fairly involved progressions that are quite difficult (even for me) to progress through.

Music and sound effects are ok - nothing special.

The developers are not native English Speakers (company is based on Russia). This shows in some awkward grammar in places and accented speech clips.

There are working steam leaderboards as well as local high scores (yes, I set #1 scores on the 3 tables I've played through so far ;).

Each table saves progress automatically, even if you kill the game or if it crashes.

There are various bugs I've encountered, some game breaking, but they're not too common. Some elements of some tables don't seem to work correctly. There's a glitch that causes serious game-breaking graphics issues occasionally if you open the help while in game and then immediately resume.
